417	// checkServiceRevision applies the gate the health and select operations share.
418	// Content validation has already happened by the time it runs, so an invalid
419	// field never reaches it. It first looks the service up (an unknown service is
420	// at revision 0) and compares revisions: a mismatch is a conflict carrying the
421	// request's expectedRevision and the actual revision, even when the service or
422	// the targeted instance is missing — both values are flagged so callers emit
423	// them even when one side is 0. With matching revisions an unknown service is
424	// not_found and carries no comparison; a registered service with an empty
425	// instance list is still returned, so it compares by its real revision rather
426	// than being treated as absent. Returning nil means the gate passed and the
427	// caller owns the rest.
428	func (r *Registry) checkServiceRevision(service string, expected int) (*serviceState, *revisionFailure) {
429		st, exists := r.services[service]
430		actual := 0
431		if exists {
432			actual = st.revision
433		}
434		if expected != actual {
435			return nil, &revisionFailure{
436				kind:     OutcomeConflict,
437				reason:   fmt.Sprintf("service %q is at revision %d, not %d", service, actual, expected),
438				revision: actual,
439				expected: expected,
440				actual:   actual,
441				mismatch: true,
442			}
443		}
444		if !exists {
445			return nil, &revisionFailure{

447				reason:   fmt.Sprintf("service %q does not exist", service),

502	// is narrowed to int. Content validity is established before any revision check.
503	func (r *Registry) ValidateRegistration(service string, revision int64, instances []Instance) (Registration, error) {
504		name, err := validateServiceName(service)
505		if err != nil {
506			return Registration{}, err
507		}
508		if err := validateExpectedRevision(revision); err != nil {
509			return Registration{}, err
510		}
511		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(instances))
512		valid := make([]Instance, 0, len(instances))
513		for _, inst := range instances {
514			id := strings.TrimSpace(inst.ID)
515			if id == "" {
516				return Registration{}, errInvalid("instance id must not be empty")
517			}
518			if seen[id] {
519				return Registration{}, errInvalid(fmt.Sprintf("duplicate instance id %q", id))
520			}
521			addr, err := parseAddress(inst.Address)
522			if err != nil {

525			seen[id] = true

531	// Apply checks the revision and, on match, replaces the service's instance list.
532	// A new service is created at revision 1 only when expectedRevision is 0.
533	// A matching registration with identical content succeeds without bumping revision.
534	//
535	// A matching registration whose normalized content differs is refused when the
536	// service is already at maxRevision: recording the change would increment the
537	// revision past the architecture's integer range, overflowing to a negative
538	// value that no valid expectedRevision could ever match again. Such a request
539	// is invalid (not a revision conflict, so it carries neither
540	// expectedRevision nor actualRevision), keeps the revision at the limit, and
541	// changes no instance, health record, rotation position or session binding.
542	// Submitting the same normalized list — a pure reorder or whitespace-only
543	// difference included — still succeeds without a revision bump.
544	func (r *Registry) Apply(reg Registration) Outcome {
545		st, exists := r.services[reg.Service]
546		if !exists {
547			if reg.Revision != 0 {
548				return Outcome{
549					Service:          reg.Service,
550					OK:               false,
551					Kind:             OutcomeConflict,
552					Reason:           fmt.Sprintf("service %q does not exist yet; expected revision must be 0, got %d", reg.Service, reg.Revision),
553					Expected:         reg.Revision,
554					Actual:           0,
555					Revision:         0,
556					RevisionMismatch: true,
557				}
558			}
559			st = &serviceState{revision: 1, instances: make(map[string]*instanceState, len(reg.Instances))}
560			r.services[reg.Service] = st
561			for _, inst := range reg.Instances {
562				st.instances[inst.ID] = newInstanceState(inst.Address)
563			}
564			return Outcome{Service: reg.Service, OK: true, Changed: true, Revision: 1}
565		}
566		if reg.Revision != st.revision {
567			return Outcome{
568				Service:          reg.Service,
569				OK:               false,
570				Kind:             OutcomeConflict,
571				Reason:           fmt.Sprintf("service %q is at revision %d, not %d", reg.Service, st.revision, reg.Revision),
572				Expected:         reg.Revision,
573				Actual:           st.revision,
574				Revision:         st.revision,
575				RevisionMismatch: true,
576			}
577		}
578		changed := !sameInstances(st.instances, reg.Instances)
579		if changed {
580			// The revision is already at the architecture's maximum: recording this
581			// change would require incrementing it, which overflows int into a
582			// negative value that no legal expectedRevision can match. Refuse the
583			// whole replacement as invalid before rebuilding the map, so the list,
584			// health records, rotation position and session bindings stay as they
585			// were.
586			if st.revision >= maxRevision {
587				return Outcome{
588					Service:  reg.Service,
589					OK:       false,
590					Kind:     OutcomeInvalid,
591					Reason:   revisionLimitReachedReason(maxRevision),
592					Revision: st.revision,
593				}
594			}
595			// A replacement fully rebuilds the list, but an instance that keeps both
596			// its id and its address retains its health observation. Anything new,
597			// address-changed, or removed-then-readded starts from unknown at sequence 0.
598			next := make(map[string]*instanceState, len(reg.Instances))
599			for _, inst := range reg.Instances {
600				if old, ok := st.instances[inst.ID]; ok && old.address == inst.Address {
601					next[inst.ID] = old
602				} else {
603					next[inst.ID] = newInstanceState(inst.Address)
604				}
605			}
606			st.instances = next
607			st.revision++
608		}
609		return Outcome{Service: reg.Service, OK: true, Changed: changed, Revision: st.revision}
610	}

612	// ValidateHealth trims and validates one health observation without mutating
613	// the registry. revision is the raw submitted expectedRevision, range-checked
614	// before it is narrowed to int. Content validity is established before any
615	// revision check.
616	func (r *Registry) ValidateHealth(service, instanceID string, revision int64, sequence int64, healthy bool, reason string) (HealthUpdate, error) {
617		name, err := validateServiceName(service)
618		if err != nil {
619			return HealthUpdate{}, err
620		}
621		id := strings.TrimSpace(instanceID)
622		if id == "" {
623			return HealthUpdate{}, errInvalid("instance id must not be empty")
624		}
625		if err := validateExpectedRevision(revision); err != nil {
626			return HealthUpdate{}, err
627		}
628		if sequence <= 0 {
629			return HealthUpdate{}, errInvalid("sequence must be a positive integer")
630		}
631		normalizedReason := strings.TrimSpace(reason)
632		if healthy {
633			// A healthy observation carries no reason.
634			normalizedReason = ""
635		} else if normalizedReason == "" {
636			return HealthUpdate{}, errInvalid("reason must not be empty when unhealthy")
637		}
638		return HealthUpdate{
639			Service:    name,
640			InstanceID: id,
641			Revision:   int(revision),
642			Sequence:   sequence,
643			Healthy:    healthy,
644			Reason:     normalizedReason,
645		}, nil
646	}

648	// ApplyHealth records an offline observation once the shared revision gate has
649	// passed.
650	//
651	// The gate is shared with Select (see checkServiceRevision): a revision
652	// mismatch is a conflict carrying the request and current revisions even when
653	// the service or the targeted instance is missing, and a matching request for
654	// an unknown service is not_found. Only after it does health apply its own
655	// rules:
656	//   - a missing instance is not_found;
657	//   - a sequence below the accepted one is stale and reports the current sequence;
658	//   - the same sequence with identical normalized status and reason succeeds
659	//     without changing state;
660	//   - the same sequence with different content is a conflict;
661	//   - a newer sequence writes the status and reason.
662	func (r *Registry) ApplyHealth(upd HealthUpdate) HealthOutcome {
663		st, fail := r.checkServiceRevision(upd.Service, upd.Revision)
664		if fail != nil {
665			return fail.asHealth(upd.Service)
666		}
667		cur, ok := st.instances[upd.InstanceID]
668		if !ok {
669			return HealthOutcome{
670				Service:    upd.Service,
671				InstanceID: upd.InstanceID,
672				OK:         false,
673				Kind:       OutcomeNotFound,
674				Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("instance %q does not exist in service %q", upd.InstanceID, upd.Service),
675				Revision:   st.revision,
676			}
677		}
678		if upd.Sequence < cur.sequence {
679			return HealthOutcome{
680				Service:    upd.Service,
681				InstanceID: upd.InstanceID,
682				OK:         false,
683				Kind:       OutcomeStale,
684				Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("sequence %d is older than the current sequence %d", upd.Sequence, cur.sequence),
685				Revision:   st.revision,
686				Sequence:   cur.sequence,
687			}
688		}
689		if upd.Sequence == cur.sequence {
690			want := HealthUnhealthy
691			if upd.Healthy {
692				want = HealthHealthy
693			}
694			if cur.health == want && cur.reason == upd.Reason {
695				return HealthOutcome{
696					Service:    upd.Service,
697					InstanceID: upd.InstanceID,
698					OK:         true,
699					Changed:    false,
700					Revision:   st.revision,
701					Sequence:   cur.sequence,
702				}
703			}
704			return HealthOutcome{
705				Service:    upd.Service,
706				InstanceID: upd.InstanceID,
707				OK:         false,
708				Kind:       OutcomeConflict,
709				Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("sequence %d already used with different health content", upd.Sequence),
710				Revision:   st.revision,
711				Sequence:   cur.sequence,
712			}
713		}
714		// Newer sequence: record the observation. Health updates never bump the
715		// registration revision.
716		if upd.Healthy {
717			cur.health = HealthHealthy
718			cur.reason = ""
719		} else {
720			cur.health = HealthUnhealthy
721			cur.reason = upd.Reason
722		}
723		cur.sequence = upd.Sequence
724		return HealthOutcome{
725			Service:    upd.Service,
726			InstanceID: upd.InstanceID,
727			OK:         true,
728			Changed:    true,
729			Revision:   st.revision,
730			Sequence:   cur.sequence,
731		}
732	}

734	// validateSessionRequest is the content validation shared by select and
735	// release_session. It trims the service name and range-checks the raw
736	// expectedRevision before it is narrowed to int, then normalizes the session
737	// key:
738	//
739	//   - a nil key means the field was absent: an ordinary rotating selection is
740	//     legal for select (keyRequired == false), while release_session rejects
741	//     it with missingKeyReason because its key is mandatory;
742	//   - a present key is trimmed; keys equal after trimming name one session
743	//     within a service, and a blank-after-trim key is invalid with a reason
744	//     naming the sessionKey problem.
745	//
746	// The order mirrors every other request kind — service name, then the
747	// revision range, then the remaining content field — so content validity is
748	// fully established before any revision comparison against the registry.
749	// Null and non-string key tokens are a JSON concern handled by callers before
750	// this helper runs and never arrive here as a *string.
751	func validateSessionRequest(service string, revision int64, sessionKey *string, keyRequired bool, missingKeyReason string) (name string, rev int, key string, err error) {
752		name, err = validateServiceName(service)
753		if err != nil {
754			return "", 0, "", err
755		}
756		if err = validateExpectedRevision(revision); err != nil {
757			return "", 0, "", err
758		}
759		if sessionKey == nil {
760			if keyRequired {
761				return "", 0, "", errInvalid(missingKeyReason)
762			}
763			return name, int(revision), "", nil
764		}
765		key = strings.TrimSpace(*sessionKey)
766		if key == "" {
767			return "", 0, "", errInvalid("sessionKey must not be empty")
768		}
769		return name, int(revision), key, nil
770	}

778	// ValidateSelectionWithSession is ValidateSelection with an optional session
779	// key. A nil key means an ordinary rotating selection. A non-nil key is
780	// trimmed and must not be blank: keys that differ only in surrounding
781	// whitespace name the same session. revision is the raw submitted
782	// expectedRevision, range-checked before it is narrowed to int. Content
783	// validity is established before any revision check.

788	// ValidateSelectionWithExclusions is ValidateSelectionWithSession with an
789	// optional excludeInstanceIds list. A nil or empty list means an ordinary
790	// selection with no exclusions. Each id is trimmed before use and duplicate
791	// ids count as one; an id that is blank after trimming is invalid with a
792	// reason naming the excludeInstanceIds problem. Ids unknown to the registry
793	// are not an error — they simply exclude nothing. revision is the raw
794	// submitted expectedRevision, range-checked before it is narrowed to int.
795	// Content validity is fully established before any revision check, so a
796	// malformed list fails the item as invalid even when its revision would also
797	// conflict, and no valid id in the list can make the failed item partially
798	// take effect.
799	func (r *Registry) ValidateSelectionWithExclusions(service string, revision int64, sessionKey *string, excludeIDs []string) (Selection, error) {
800		name, rev, key, err := validateSessionRequest(service, revision, sessionKey, false, "")
801		if err != nil {
802			return Selection{}, err
803		}
804		excludes, err := normalizeExcludeIDs(excludeIDs)
805		if err != nil {
806			return Selection{}, err
807		}
808		return Selection{Service: name, Revision: rev, SessionKey: key, ExcludeIDs: excludes}, nil
809	}

811	// normalizeExcludeIDs trims and deduplicates one excludeInstanceIds list.
812	// Each id is trimmed of surrounding whitespace before it names an instance;
813	// ids equal after trimming name the same instance and are kept once. An id
814	// that is blank after trimming is invalid with a reason naming the
815	// excludeInstanceIds problem. A nil or empty list normalizes to nil, which
816	// selects exactly as if the field had never been submitted.
817	func normalizeExcludeIDs(raw []string) ([]string, error) {
818		if len(raw) == 0 {
819			return nil, nil
820		}
821		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(raw))
822		ids := make([]string, 0, len(raw))
823		for _, id := range raw {
824			id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
825			if id == "" {
826				return nil, errInvalid("excludeInstanceIds must not contain an empty instance id")
827			}
828			if seen[id] {
829				continue
830			}
831			seen[id] = true
832			ids = append(ids, id)
833		}
834		return ids, nil
835	}

837	// ValidateSessionRelease trims and validates one release_session request
838	// without touching the registry. Unlike a selection the sessionKey is
839	// mandatory: a nil (absent) key or a blank-after-trim key is invalid with a
840	// reason naming the sessionKey problem. revision is the raw submitted
841	// expectedRevision, range-checked before it is narrowed to int. The check
842	// order mirrors ValidateSelectionWithSession — service name, then the
843	// revision range, then the key — and content validity is fully established
844	// before any revision comparison against the registry.
845	func (r *Registry) ValidateSessionRelease(service string, revision int64, sessionKey *string) (SessionRelease, error) {
846		const missingKeyReason = "sessionKey is required and must be a non-empty string"
847		name, rev, key, err := validateSessionRequest(service, revision, sessionKey, true, missingKeyReason)
848		if err != nil {
849			return SessionRelease{}, err
850		}
851		return SessionRelease{Service: name, Revision: rev, SessionKey: key}, nil
852	}

854	// Select chooses one healthy instance for the service once the shared revision
855	// gate has passed.
856	//
857	// The gate is shared with ApplyHealth (see checkServiceRevision): a mismatch is
858	// a conflict carrying the request and current revisions (an unknown service is
859	// at revision 0), and a matching request for an unknown service is not_found.
860	// Only after it does select apply its own rule: an existing service with no
861	// healthy instance is no_healthy and no address is fabricated. A registered
862	// service with an empty instance list still compares by its real revision; the
863	// gate hands it through so the answer is no_healthy, not not_found.
864	//
865	// Healthy instances rotate per service by ascending instance id: the first
866	// success takes the smallest id and each later success continues just after
867	// the previously chosen id, wrapping to the smallest id past the end. With a
868	// single healthy instance it may be chosen repeatedly. Registrations and
869	// health changes alter the candidate set immediately but never reset the
870	// rotation; failed selections leave the cursor where it was.
871	//
872	// A request carrying a session key is sticky: while the key's bound instance
873	// is still registered and healthy at selection time, it is returned with its
874	// current address and latest accepted health sequence, and the rotation
875	// cursor does not move. A binding that points at a removed, unknown or
876	// unhealthy instance is ignored — an instance whose id survived an address
877	// change is unknown until a fresh observation at the new address, so its old
878	// health record never carries over — and the request falls back to the normal
879	// rotation, which on success advances the cursor and replaces the binding.
880	// The first selection for a key behaves exactly like an ordinary rotation
881	// success and additionally records the binding. Failed selections (including
882	// no_healthy) create no binding, rewrite none and move no cursor.
883	//
884	// A request carrying excludeInstanceIds skips the listed ids for this one
885	// request only: an excluded instance keeps its registration and health record
886	// and a later request without the list may choose it again. The exclusion
887	// filters the healthy candidate set before the rotation runs, so the rotation
888	// still continues just after the last actually rotated id — excluding that id
889	// does not reset the position, the next non-excluded healthy id after it is
890	// chosen, and only when none follows does the rotation wrap to the smallest
891	// candidate. A bound session whose instance is excluded falls back to this
892	// filtered rotation exactly as if the instance were unhealthy, rebinding only
893	// that key on success while every other session keeps its binding. When the
894	// service has healthy instances but every one of them is excluded, the
895	// no_healthy reason says the exclusion removed them all; when there is no
896	// healthy instance at all, the reason is the ordinary one. Either failure
897	// fabricates no target and moves nothing.
898	func (r *Registry) Select(sel Selection) SelectOutcome {
899		st, fail := r.checkServiceRevision(sel.Service, sel.Revision)
900		if fail != nil {
901			return fail.asSelect(sel.Service)
902		}
903	
904		excluded := make(map[string]bool, len(sel.ExcludeIDs))
905		for _, id := range sel.ExcludeIDs {
906			excluded[id] = true
907		}
908	
909		// A bound session reuses its instance while it is registered, healthy and
910		// not excluded by this request; the reuse reflects the instance's current
911		// address and sequence and does not advance the rotation.
912		if sel.SessionKey != "" {
913			if id, bound := st.sessions[sel.SessionKey]; bound {
914				if cur, ok := st.instances[id]; ok && cur.health == HealthHealthy && !excluded[id] {
915					return SelectOutcome{
916						Service:    sel.Service,
917						OK:         true,
918						Revision:   st.revision,
919						InstanceID: id,
920						Address:    cur.address,
921						Sequence:   cur.sequence,
922					}
923				}
924			}
925		}
926	
927		healthy := make([]string, 0, len(st.instances))
928		for id, cur := range st.instances {
929			if cur.health == HealthHealthy {
930				healthy = append(healthy, id)
931			}
932		}
933		sort.Strings(healthy)
934	
935		candidates := healthy[:0]
936		for _, id := range healthy {
937			if !excluded[id] {
938				candidates = append(candidates, id)
939			}
940		}
941		if len(candidates) == 0 {
942			reason := fmt.Sprintf("service %q has no healthy instance available", sel.Service)
943			if len(healthy) > 0 {
944				reason = fmt.Sprintf("service %q has no healthy instance available: all healthy instances are excluded by excludeInstanceIds", sel.Service)
945			}
946			return SelectOutcome{
947				Service:  sel.Service,
948				OK:       false,
949				Kind:     OutcomeNoHealthy,
950				Reason:   reason,
951				Revision: st.revision,
952			}
953		}
954	
955		chosen := candidates[0]
956		if st.cursorSet {
957			chosen = candidates[0]
958			for _, id := range candidates {
959				if id > st.cursor {
960					chosen = id
961					break
962				}
963			}
964		}
965		cur := st.instances[chosen]
966		st.cursor = chosen
967		st.cursorSet = true
968		if sel.SessionKey != "" {
969			if st.sessions == nil {
970				st.sessions = make(map[string]string)
971			}
972			st.sessions[sel.SessionKey] = chosen
973		}
974		return SelectOutcome{
975			Service:    sel.Service,
976			OK:         true,
977			Revision:   st.revision,
978			InstanceID: chosen,
979			Address:    cur.address,
980			Sequence:   cur.sequence,
981		}
982	}
983	
984	// ReleaseSession drops one session binding once the shared revision gate has
985	// passed.
986	//
987	// The gate is the same one health and select use (see
988	// checkServiceRevision): a revision mismatch is a conflict carrying the
989	// request and current revisions (an unknown service is at revision 0), and a
990	// matching request for an unknown service is not_found — including when
991	// expectedRevision is 0. Only after it does release do its own work.
992	//
993	// Releasing deletes at most the named key's binding in the named service. It
994	// never consults the bound instance's state: whether that instance was
995	// removed, never observed healthy, is currently unknown/unhealthy, or the
996	// service's instance list is empty cannot keep the binding in place, since
997	// the binding is only a remembered id. Releasing a key that has no binding
998	// still succeeds with Changed left false. No target is chosen, so the result
999	// carries no instance id, address or health sequence.
1000	//
1001	// The release moves and resets neither the rotation cursor nor any other
1002	// session's binding (including another session bound to the same instance and
1003	// the same key in another service), and it never alters the instance list,
1004	// the registration revision or a health record. The next selection with the
1005	// released key follows the first-binding rule: it rotates from just after the
1006	// last actually rotated position and records a fresh binding only on success.
1007	func (r *Registry) ReleaseSession(rel SessionRelease) ReleaseOutcome {
1008		st, fail := r.checkServiceRevision(rel.Service, rel.Revision)
1009		if fail != nil {
1010			return fail.asRelease(rel.Service)
1011		}
1012		_, bound := st.sessions[rel.SessionKey]
1013		if bound {
1014			delete(st.sessions, rel.SessionKey)
1015		}
1016		return ReleaseOutcome{
1017			Service:  rel.Service,
1018			OK:       true,
1019			Changed:  bound,
1020			Revision: st.revision,
1021		}
1022	}

1024	// Snapshot returns all services sorted by name, with instances sorted by id.
1025	func (r *Registry) Snapshot() []ServiceView {
1026		names := make([]string, 0, len(r.services))
1027		for name := range r.services {
1028			names = append(names, name)
1029		}
1030		sort.Strings(names)
1031		views := make([]ServiceView, 0, len(names))
1032		for _, name := range names {
1033			st := r.services[name]

1068	// A domain host may end in exactly one root dot (e.g. "api.example.:8080"),
1069	// which is retained in the returned text. No network I/O is performed.
1070	func parseAddress(raw string) (string, error) {
1071		addr := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
1072		if addr == "" {
1073			return "", fmt.Errorf("instance address must not be empty")
1074		}
1075		for _, r := range addr {
1076			if unicode.IsSpace(r) || unicode.IsControl(r) {
1077				return "", fmt.Errorf("instance address %q must not contain whitespace or control characters", addr)
1078			}
1079		}
1080		host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(addr)
1081		if err != nil {
1082			return "", fmt.Errorf("instance address %q is not a host:port address: %v", addr, err)
1083		}
1084		if host == "" {
1085			return "", fmt.Errorf("instance address %q has an empty host", addr)
1086		}
1087		if !allDigits(port) {

1093		}
1094		if n < 1 || n > 65535 {
1095			return "", fmt.Errorf("instance address %q port %d is out of range (1-65535)", addr, n)
1096		}
1097		if strings.HasPrefix(addr, "[") {
1098			ip := net.ParseIP(host)
1099			if ip == nil || !strings.Contains(host, ":") {
1100				return "", fmt.Errorf("instance address %q bracketed host is not a valid IPv6 address", addr)
1101			}
1102		} else if ip := net.ParseIP(host); ip != nil {
1103			if ip.To4() == nil {

1105			}
1106		} else if !isDomainName(host) {

1108		}

1110	}

1112	func allDigits(s string) bool {
1113		if s == "" {
1114			return false
1115		}
1116		for _, r := range s {
1117			if r < '0' || r > '9' {
1118				return false
1119			}
1120		}
1121		return true
1122	}
1123	
1124	// isDomainName validates a dotted hostname with alphanumeric/hyphen labels.
1125	// A domain may be written in its fully qualified form ending in exactly one
1126	// root dot (e.g. "api.example."): the trailing dot marks the DNS root rather
1127	// than separating two labels, so it is not itself a label, is not counted in
1128	// the 253-character body limit, and no second trailing dot is allowed. An
1129	// empty body (".") or any empty label in the body ("a..b.", "a.b..") is
1130	// rejected just like any other malformed label. No name resolution occurs.
1131	func isDomainName(host string) bool {
1132		body := host
1133		if strings.HasSuffix(body, ".") {
1134			body = body[:len(body)-1]
1135		}
1136		if body == "" || len(body) > 253 {
1137			return false
1138		}
1139		for _, label := range strings.Split(body, ".") {
1140			n := len(label)
1141			if n == 0 || n > 63 {
1142				return false
1143			}
1144			if label[0] == '-' || label[n-1] == '-' {
1145				return false
1146			}
1147			for _, r := range label {
1148				if r == '-' ||
1149					(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') ||
1150					(r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') ||
1151					(r >= '0' && r <= '9') {
1152					continue
1153				}
1154				return false
1155			}
1156		}
1157		return true
1158	}

93	// same-sequence health-content conflict is also "conflict" but is not a
94	// revision mismatch, so it omits both fields exactly like invalid,
95	// not_found, stale and no_healthy.
96	type registerResult struct {
97		Service          string `json:"service"`
98		OK               bool   `json:"ok"`

100		Revision         int    `json:"revision"`

116	// runRegister processes registration requests from the process standard
117	// streams. It returns the process exit code: 0 when all registrations succeed
118	// and the result is fully written, 1 otherwise.

123	// runRegisterIO is runRegister with injectable streams. in supplies the JSON
124	// request batch, out receives the single JSON result document and errOut
125	// receives diagnostics (in particular a result-delivery failure, which must
126	// never be mixed into out).
127	func runRegisterIO(in io.Reader, out io.Writer, errOut io.Writer) int {
128		data, err := io.ReadAll(in)
129		if err != nil {
130			return failRegister(out, errOut, fmt.Sprintf("could not read standard input: %v", err))
131		}
132	
133		var top struct {
134			Requests json.RawMessage `json:"requests"`
135		}

137			return failRegister(out, errOut, fmt.Sprintf("input must be a JSON object with a requests array: %v", err))
138		}
139		if len(top.Requests) == 0 || strings.TrimSpace(string(top.Requests)) == "null" {
140			return failRegister(out, errOut, "input must contain a \"requests\" array")
141		}
142		var rawRequests []json.RawMessage
143		if err := json.Unmarshal(top.Requests, &rawRequests); err != nil {
144			return failRegister(out, errOut, "\"requests\" must be a JSON array")
145		}
146	
147		proc := &registerProcessor{
148			registry: indexroom.NewRegistry(),
149			results:  make([]registerResult, 0, len(rawRequests)),
150		}
151	
152		for _, raw := range rawRequests {
153			var head struct {
154				Service string          `json:"service"`
155				Type    json.RawMessage `json:"type"`
156			}
157			_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &head)
158			service := strings.TrimSpace(head.Service)

161			if len(head.Type) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(string(head.Type)) != "null" {

170			switch reqType {

175			case "select":

177			case "release_session":

180				proc.invalidf(service, "unknown type %q", reqType)
181			}
182		}

185		registry := proc.registry

187		services := make([]registerService, 0)

229	// checked before any business rule, so the revision stamped here is the
230	// service's current revision when the item is handled.
231	func (p *registerProcessor) invalid(service, reason string) {

235			OK:       false,
236			Error:    "invalid",

253	// parseRevision decodes the raw expectedRevision token for one request. An

260	// the item's invalid result, which stamps the service's current revision.
261	// Every request kind shares this check, so the missing/null reason and its
262	// precedence live here rather than at each call site.
263	func (p *registerProcessor) parseRevision(service string, raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
264		if revisionMissing(raw) {

315	// expectedRevision is the required-field error first; once the revision token

317	// type error (never "no key submitted"), and only then is the revision parsed
318	// as an integer. An omitted sessionKey arrives as nil: select's validator
319	// treats it as an ordinary rotating selection, while release_session's
320	// validator rejects it as a sessionKey problem — each after the service-name
321	// and revision-range checks, so a simultaneously bad revision still precedes

324	// and a blank-after-trim key loses to nothing but a service-name or
325	// revision-range problem. On failure the item's invalid result is appended and

329		var req struct {
330			Service  string          `json:"service"`
331			Revision json.RawMessage `json:"expectedRevision"`

340	
341		if revisionMissing(req.Revision) {
342			p.invalid(service, "expectedRevision is required and must be a non-negative integer")

344		}
345	
346		// An explicit null or a non-string token names a sessionKey type problem
347		// for either request kind; it is judged once the revision token is known
348		// present and before the revision is parsed. An omitted field stays nil and
349		// reaches the operation's own validator, which distinguishes an ordinary
350		// keyless select from release_session's mandatory key.
351		var sessionKey *string
352		if len(req.Session) > 0 {
353			if strings.TrimSpace(string(req.Session)) == "null" {
354				p.invalid(service, "sessionKey must be a string, not null")

363		}
364	
365		revision, ok := p.parseRevision(service, req.Revision)
366		if !ok {
367			return sessionRequestInput{}, false
368		}
369		return sessionRequestInput{service: service, revision: revision, sessionKey: sessionKey, excludeIDs: req.Exclude}, true
370	}
371	
372	// parseExcludeIDs decodes the raw excludeInstanceIds token of one select
373	// request. An omitted field (and only that) yields a nil list, which selects
374	// exactly as before; an explicit null, a non-array token or a non-string
375	// element becomes this item's own invalid result with a reason naming the
376	// excludeInstanceIds problem, so one malformed list neither aborts the batch
377	// nor partially applies alongside the valid ids it also carried. The elements
378	// are returned as submitted — trimming, deduplication and the blank-id rule
379	// belong to the registry's validator, which runs them before any revision
380	// comparison just like the sessionKey checks. It reports false after
381	// appending the item's invalid result, which stamps the service's current
382	// revision.
383	func (p *registerProcessor) parseExcludeIDs(service string, raw json.RawMessage) ([]string, bool) {
384		if len(raw) == 0 {
385			return nil, true
386		}
387		if strings.TrimSpace(string(raw)) == "null" {
388			p.invalid(service, "excludeInstanceIds must be an array of strings, not null")
389			return nil, false
390		}
391		if !isJSONArray(raw) {
392			p.invalid(service, "excludeInstanceIds must be an array of strings")
393			return nil, false
394		}
395		var elements []json.RawMessage
396		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &elements); err != nil {
397			p.invalidf(service, "excludeInstanceIds must be an array of strings: %v", err)
398			return nil, false
399		}
400		ids := make([]string, 0, len(elements))
401		for _, element := range elements {
402			var id string
403			if err := json.Unmarshal(element, &id); err != nil {
404				p.invalid(service, "excludeInstanceIds must contain only strings")
405				return nil, false
406			}
407			ids = append(ids, id)
408		}
409		return ids, true
410	}
411	
412	// reject records a business-rule failure (conflict, not_found, stale or
413	// no_healthy), keeping each operation's distinct result fields. expected and
414	// actual are attached as present JSON integers only when revisionConflict is
415	// set — a registration-revision mismatch, where either side can be 0 (a
416	// new-service request submits 0; an unknown service is at 0). A health
417	// same-sequence/different-content conflict is also "conflict" but passes
418	// false, so the comparison fields stay omitted and it cannot be mistaken for
419	// a registration mismatch. Health rejections additionally carry the current
420	// sequence; the other operations pass 0 so it stays omitted.
421	func (p *registerProcessor) reject(service string, kind indexroom.OutcomeKind, reason string, revision, expected, actual int, revisionConflict bool, sequence int64) {
422		p.failed = true
423		result := registerResult{
424			Service:  service,
425			OK:       false,
426			Error:    string(kind),
427			Reason:   reason,
428			Revision: revision,
429			Sequence: sequence,
430		}
431		if revisionConflict {
432			// Take distinct heap copies: zero is an expected value here and must
433			// serialize as 0 rather than being dropped by omitempty.
434			submitted, current := expected, actual
435			result.ExpectedRevision = &submitted
436			result.ActualRevision = &current
437		}
438		p.results = append(p.results, result)
439	}
440	
441	// succeed records an accepted item; omitempty keeps zero-valued fields out of
442	// the output exactly as before the refactor.
443	func (p *registerProcessor) succeed(result registerResult) {
444		result.OK = true
445		p.results = append(p.results, result)
446	}
447	
448	// registerRequest processes one register request, appending its outcome.
449	func (p *registerProcessor) registerRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
450		var req struct {
451			Service   string          `json:"service"`
452			Revision  json.RawMessage `json:"expectedRevision"`
453			Instances json.RawMessage `json:"instances"`
454		}
455		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &req); err != nil {
456			p.invalidf(service, "request must be an object with service, expectedRevision and instances: %v", err)
457			return
458		}
459		service = strings.TrimSpace(req.Service)
460	
461		if revisionMissing(req.Revision) {
462			p.invalid(service, "expectedRevision is required and must be a non-negative integer")
463			return
464		}
465		if !isJSONArray(req.Instances) {
466			p.invalid(service, "instances must be an array")
467			return
468		}
469		var instances []indexroom.Instance
470		if err := json.Unmarshal(req.Instances, &instances); err != nil {
471			p.invalidf(service, "instances must be an array of objects with id and address: %v", err)
472			return
473		}
474	
475		// Parse the raw token (integer type); ValidateRegistration then range-checks
476		// the int64 against the architecture before narrowing it to int.
477		revision, ok := p.parseRevision(service, req.Revision)
478		if !ok {
479			return
480		}
481		registration, err := p.registry.ValidateRegistration(service, revision, instances)
482		if err != nil {
483			p.invalid(service, err.Error())
484			return
485		}
486	
487		outcome := p.registry.Apply(registration)
488		if !outcome.OK {
489			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, outcome.RevisionMismatch, 0)
490			return
491		}
492		p.succeed(registerResult{
493			Service:  outcome.Service,
494			Changed:  outcome.Changed,
495			Revision: outcome.Revision,
496		})
497	}
498	
499	// healthRequest processes one health observation request, appending its outcome.
500	func (p *registerProcessor) healthRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
501		var req struct {
502			Service    string          `json:"service"`
503			InstanceID string          `json:"instanceId"`
504			Revision   json.RawMessage `json:"expectedRevision"`
505			Sequence   json.RawMessage `json:"sequence"`
506			Healthy    *bool           `json:"healthy"`
507			Reason     *string         `json:"reason"`
508		}
509		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &req); err != nil {
510			p.invalidf(service, "health request must be an object with service, instanceId, expectedRevision, sequence and healthy: %v", err)
511			return
512		}
513		service = strings.TrimSpace(req.Service)
514	
515		if revisionMissing(req.Revision) {
516			p.invalid(service, "expectedRevision is required and must be a non-negative integer")
517			return
518		}
519		if len(req.Sequence) == 0 || strings.TrimSpace(string(req.Sequence)) == "null" {
520			p.invalid(service, "sequence is required and must be a positive integer")
521			return
522		}
523		if req.Healthy == nil {
524			p.invalid(service, "healthy is required and must be a boolean")
525			return
526		}
527		reason := ""
528		if req.Reason != nil {
529			reason = *req.Reason
530		}
531	
532		// Parse the raw tokens (integer type); ValidateHealth then range-checks
533		// the revision against the architecture before narrowing it to int, while
534		// a non-integer or out-of-range sequence becomes this item's own invalid
535		// result carrying a sequence-specific reason rather than a decode error.
536		revision, ok := p.parseRevision(service, req.Revision)
537		if !ok {
538			return
539		}
540		sequence, ok := p.parseSequence(service, req.Sequence)
541		if !ok {
542			return
543		}
544		update, err := p.registry.ValidateHealth(service, req.InstanceID, revision, sequence, *req.Healthy, reason)
545		if err != nil {
546			p.invalid(service, err.Error())
547			return
548		}
549	
550		outcome := p.registry.ApplyHealth(update)
551		if !outcome.OK {
552			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, outcome.RevisionMismatch, outcome.Sequence)
553			return
554		}
555		p.succeed(registerResult{
556			Service:  outcome.Service,
557			Changed:  outcome.Changed,
558			Revision: outcome.Revision,
559			Sequence: outcome.Sequence,
560		})
561	}
562	
563	// selectRequest processes one select request, appending its outcome.
564	// A selection performs no network access and never alters registrations or
565	// health records; it only advances the service's healthy-instance rotation
566	// and, for requests carrying a sessionKey, maintains that session's binding.
567	// An optional excludeInstanceIds array of strings skips the listed instances
568	// for this one request without touching their registration or health records.
569	func (p *registerProcessor) selectRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
570		in, ok := p.readSessionRequest(raw, service,
571			"select request must be an object with service and expectedRevision: %v")
572		if !ok {
573			return
574		}
575	
576		// The exclude list is decoded after the shared session/revision token
577		// handling and validated by the registry before any revision comparison,
578		// so a malformed list is this item's own invalid result and never a
579		// conflict, and the valid ids it also carried cannot partially apply.
580		excludeIDs, ok := p.parseExcludeIDs(in.service, in.excludeIDs)
581		if !ok {
582			return
583		}
584	
585		// readSessionRequest delivered the parsed revision and the key as decoded
586		// (nil for an omitted key); ValidateSelectionWithExclusions repeats the
587		// shared service/revision/key content checks via the registry, trims the
588		// key, and normalizes the exclude list (trimming, deduplicating and
589		// rejecting blank ids).
590		selection, err := p.registry.ValidateSelectionWithExclusions(in.service, in.revision, in.sessionKey, excludeIDs)
591		if err != nil {
592			p.invalid(in.service, err.Error())
593			return
594		}
595	
596		outcome := p.registry.Select(selection)
597		if !outcome.OK {
598			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, outcome.RevisionMismatch, 0)
599			return
600		}
601		p.succeed(registerResult{
602			Service:    outcome.Service,
603			Revision:   outcome.Revision,
604			InstanceID: outcome.InstanceID,
605			Address:    outcome.Address,
606			Sequence:   outcome.Sequence,
607		})
608	}
609	
610	// releaseSessionRequest processes one release_session request, appending its
611	// outcome. The request releases one session binding in one service: it never
612	// selects a target, never moves the rotation cursor or any other binding, and
613	// never alters the instance list, revision or health records. A present
614	// binding is removed and reported changed; releasing an unbound key still
615	// succeeds without changed.
616	func (p *registerProcessor) releaseSessionRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
617		in, ok := p.readSessionRequest(raw, service,
618			"release_session request must be an object with service, expectedRevision and sessionKey: %v")
619		if !ok {
620			return
621		}
622	
623		// The key is mandatory for release: readSessionRequest rejects an explicit
624		// null or non-string key, and an omitted key reaches ValidateSessionRelease
625		// as nil and is rejected there after the service-name and revision-range
626		// checks. The validator also trims the key and rejects a blank one before
627		// any revision comparison against the registry.
628		release, err := p.registry.ValidateSessionRelease(in.service, in.revision, in.sessionKey)
629		if err != nil {
630			p.invalid(in.service, err.Error())
631			return
632		}
633	
634		outcome := p.registry.ReleaseSession(release)
635		if !outcome.OK {
636			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, outcome.RevisionMismatch, 0)
637			return
638		}
639		p.succeed(registerResult{
640			Service:  outcome.Service,
641			Changed:  outcome.Changed,
642			Revision: outcome.Revision,
643		})
644	}
645	
646	// failRegister emits a top-level input error as the single JSON document on
647	// out and returns exit code 1. If that error JSON itself cannot be written,
648	// the delivery failure is diagnosed on errOut (out may already hold a partial
649	// document, so no second JSON is appended) and the exit code stays 1.
650	func failRegister(out io.Writer, errOut io.Writer, reason string) int {
651		if err := writeRegisterOutput(out, struct {
652			Error string `json:"error"`
653		}{Error: reason}); err != nil {
654			reportRegisterDeliveryFailure(errOut, err)
655		}
656		return 1
657	}
658	
659	// reportRegisterDeliveryFailure reports on errOut that the register command's
660	// JSON result could not be delivered, preserving the underlying write error.
661	// It never writes to standard output, which may already contain a partial
662	// result.
663	func reportRegisterDeliveryFailure(errOut io.Writer, err error) {
664		fmt.Fprintf(errOut, "register: failed to write request results to standard output: %v\n", err)
665	}
666	
667	// writeRegisterOutput writes v as the single indented JSON document on w.
668	// Standard output is dedicated to this document, so a write failure is returned
669	// instead of swallowed: the caller must not attempt to append another document
670	// after a partial write.
671	func writeRegisterOutput(w io.Writer, v any) error {
672		enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
673		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
674		return enc.Encode(v)
675	}
676	
677	// isJSONArray reports whether raw is a JSON array (ignoring leading whitespace).
678	func isJSONArray(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
679		for _, b := range raw {
680			switch b {
681			case ' ', '\t', '\n', '\r':
682				continue
683			case '[':
684				return true
685			default:
686				return false
687			}
688		}
689		return false
690	}
691

694		blocks := []indexroom.Block{
695			{Height: 1, Hash: "h1", Parent: "genesis", Txs: []string{"t1", "t2"}},
696			{Height: 2, Hash: "h2", Parent: "h1", Txs: []string{"t3"}},
697		}
698		for _, block := range blocks {
699			if err := index.Append(block); err != nil {
700				fmt.Printf("append refused at height %d: %v\n", block.Height, err)
701				continue
702			}
703			fmt.Printf("indexed height=%d txs=%d\n", block.Height, len(block.Txs))
704		}
705		if err := index.Append(indexroom.Block{Height: 3, Hash: "h3", Parent: "h1"}); err != nil {
706			fmt.Println("non-linear block refused:", err)
707		}
708		dropped, err := index.Reorg([]indexroom.Block{{Height: 2, Hash: "h2b", Parent: "h1", Txs: []string{"t4", "t5"}}})
709		fmt.Printf("reorg dropped=%v err=%v tip=%d\n", dropped, err, index.Tip)
710	}

3	import (
4		"strings"
5		"testing"
6	)

8	// This file is the regression guard for the select request's optional
9	// excludeInstanceIds list. The list scopes one request only: excluded
10	// instances stay registered with their health records and remain eligible for
11	// later requests that carry no list. These tests lock the contract purely
12	// through the public validation, selection and snapshot results:
13	//
14	//   - the rotation still continues just after the last actually rotated id,
15	//     skipping excluded ids without resetting the position, and wraps to the
16	//     smallest candidate only when no candidate follows;
17	//   - a session whose bound instance is excluded falls back to the filtered
18	//     rotation and rebinds only its own key on success, while other sessions
19	//     keep their bindings;
20	//   - excluding every healthy instance is no_healthy with a reason naming the
21	//     exclusion, and failures move neither the cursor nor any binding;
22	//   - the list is trimmed and deduplicated, unknown ids are ignored, a blank
23	//     id is invalid naming excludeInstanceIds, and field validation precedes
24	//     the revision check.
25	
26	// selectExcluding validates and runs one select carrying an excludeInstanceIds
27	// list (and optionally a session key), returning the outcome so failure cases
28	// can be asserted directly instead of failing the helper.
29	func selectExcluding(t *testing.T, r *Registry, service string, revision int64, key *string, excludes ...string) SelectOutcome {
30		t.Helper()
31		sel, err := r.ValidateSelectionWithExclusions(service, revision, key, excludes)
32		if err != nil {
33			t.Fatalf("validate select excludes %v: %v", excludes, err)
34		}
35		return r.Select(sel)
36	}
37	
38	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeRotatesPastExcludedIDs locks the spec's rotation
39	// example: with the cursor resting on a and a, b, c all healthy, excluding b
40	// chooses c, the next plain selection wraps to a, and the one after chooses
41	// the previously excluded b — the exclusion neither resets the position nor
42	// removes the instance from later rotations.
43	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeRotatesPastExcludedIDs(t *testing.T) {
44		r := NewRegistry()
45		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
46			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
47		})
48		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
49		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
50		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")
51	
52		// Park the cursor on a with an ordinary first selection.
53		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 1)
54	
55		// Excluding b skips it for this one request: the rotation continues just
56		// after a and lands on c.
57		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil, "b"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
58	
59		// Plain selections are unaffected by the earlier exclusion: from c the
60		// rotation wraps to a, then continues to b — the excluded instance was
61		// never removed and rejoins the rotation in id order.
62		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 1)
63		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 2)
64	}
65	
66	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeLastChosenKeepsCursor locks that excluding the
67	// instance the cursor rests on does not reset the rotation: the next
68	// non-excluded healthy id after the cursor is chosen, wrapping only past the
69	// end. It also locks that the exclusion changes no registration state: the
70	// excluded instance keeps its health record and the revision stays put.
71	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeLastChosenKeepsCursor(t *testing.T) {
72		r := NewRegistry()
73		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
74			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
75		})
76		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 5, true, "")
77		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 6, true, "")
78	
79		// Cursor rests on a after the first rotation.
80		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 5)
81	
82		// Excluding a — the last actually rotated id — still continues just after
83		// it, choosing b; the position is not restarted at the smallest id.
84		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil, "a"), "b", "h2:2", 6)
85	
86		// Excluding b (now the cursor) wraps past the end to a, the only other
87		// candidate.
88		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil, "b"), "a", "h1:1", 5)
89	
90		// The exclusions changed nothing durable: both instances keep their
91		// accepted health records and the revision never moved.
92		if rev := r.RevisionOf("svc"); rev != 1 {
93			t.Fatalf("exclusion changed the registration revision: %d", rev)
94		}
95		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "a"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 5 {
96			t.Fatalf("a record changed by exclusion: %+v", inst)
97		}
98		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "b"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 6 {
99			t.Fatalf("b record changed by exclusion: %+v", inst)
100		}
101	}
102	
103	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeSessionFallbackRebindsOnlyThatKey locks the session
104	// interaction: a bound instance that is excluded is treated like an
105	// unavailable one — the request falls back to the filtered rotation, rebinds
106	// only its own key on success and advances the cursor, while another session
107	// bound elsewhere keeps its binding. A later request without the list reuses
108	// the new binding, and excluding the new binding falls back again.
109	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeSessionFallbackRebindsOnlyThatKey(t *testing.T) {
110		r := NewRegistry()
111		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
112			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
113		})
114		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
115		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
116		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")
117	
118		// x -> a, then y -> b; the shared cursor rests on b.
119		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
120		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
121	
122		// x excludes its own bound instance a: the request cannot reuse a and
123		// falls back to the rotation just after b, choosing c among the
124		// non-excluded candidates {b, c}. Only x's binding moves, to c, and the
125		// cursor advances with this real rotation.
126		keyX := "x"
127		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, &keyX, "a"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
128	
129		// y is unaffected: its own binding to b is still returned, and the reuse
130		// does not move the cursor.
131		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
132	
133		// x without a list reuses the new binding c; the exclusion was scoped to
134		// the one request that carried it.
135		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
136	
137		// A plain select continues just after the last real rotation (c) and
138		// wraps to a — the excluded instance is fully eligible again.
139		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 1)
140	
141		// Excluding x's new binding c falls back again: from the cursor on a the
142		// filtered candidates {a, b} yield b, and only x rebinds.
143		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, &keyX, "c"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
144		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
145		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
146	}
147	
148	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeAllHealthyIsNoHealthy locks the failure shape when
149	// the exclusion removes every healthy instance: no_healthy at the current
150	// revision with a reason that says the exclusion did it, no fabricated
151	// target, and no movement of the cursor or any session binding. It also locks
152	// that a service with no healthy instance at all keeps the ordinary reason
153	// even when a list is submitted.
154	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeAllHealthyIsNoHealthy(t *testing.T) {
155		r := NewRegistry()
156		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
157			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
158		})
159		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
160		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
161	
162		// x -> a; the cursor rests on a.
163		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
164	
165		assertAllExcluded := func(out SelectOutcome) {
166			t.Helper()
167			if out.OK || out.Kind != OutcomeNoHealthy {
168				t.Fatalf("should be no_healthy, got %+v", out)
169			}
170			if out.Revision != 1 {
171				t.Fatalf("no_healthy must report the current revision, got %+v", out)
172			}
173			if !strings.Contains(out.Reason, "excludeInstanceIds") {
174				t.Fatalf("reason must say the exclusion removed every healthy instance, got %q", out.Reason)
175			}
176			if out.InstanceID != "" || out.Address != "" || out.Sequence != 0 {
177				t.Fatalf("no_healthy must fabricate no target, got id=%q addr=%q seq=%d", out.InstanceID, out.Address, out.Sequence)
178			}
179		}
180	
181		// Plain and keyed requests excluding every healthy instance fail the same
182		// way; the keyed failure must not rewrite x's binding.
183		assertAllExcluded(selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil, "a", "b"))
184		keyX := "x"
185		assertAllExcluded(selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, &keyX, "b", "a"))
186	
187		// The failures moved nothing: the plain rotation still continues just
188		// after a to b, and x still reuses its preserved binding a.
189		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 2)
190		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
191	
192		// With no healthy instance at all, a submitted list does not change the
193		// ordinary no_healthy reason.
194		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 3, false, "down")
195		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 4, false, "down")
196		out := selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil, "a")
197		if out.OK || out.Kind != OutcomeNoHealthy {
198			t.Fatalf("should be no_healthy, got %+v", out)
199		}
200		if strings.Contains(out.Reason, "excludeInstanceIds") {
201			t.Fatalf("no healthy instance at all must keep the ordinary reason, got %q", out.Reason)
202		}
203	}
204	
205	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeValidation locks the list's field rules: ids are
206	// trimmed and deduplicated, unknown ids are ignored, an empty list selects
207	// exactly as if the field were absent, a blank-after-trim id is invalid with
208	// a reason naming excludeInstanceIds, and the check runs before any revision
209	// comparison so a bad list can never partially apply.
210	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeValidation(t *testing.T) {
211		r := NewRegistry()
212		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
213			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
214		})
215		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
216		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
217		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")
218	
219		// A blank-after-trim id is invalid and names the excludeInstanceIds
220		// problem; the valid ids alongside it cannot make the item apply.
221		for _, excludes := range [][]string{{"  "}, {"b", " ", "c"}} {
222			if _, err := r.ValidateSelectionWithExclusions("svc", 1, nil, excludes); err == nil {
223				t.Fatalf("excludes %v should be invalid", excludes)
224			} else if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "excludeInstanceIds") {
225				t.Fatalf("reason must name excludeInstanceIds, got %q", err)
226			}
227		}
228	
229		// The blank-id check precedes the revision comparison: a bad list with a
230		// mismatching revision is still invalid, never a conflict.
231		if _, err := r.ValidateSelectionWithExclusions("svc", 99, nil, []string{"\t"}); err == nil {
232			t.Fatalf("blank id with wrong revision should still be invalid")
233		} else if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "excludeInstanceIds") {
234			t.Fatalf("reason must name excludeInstanceIds, got %q", err)
235		}
236	
237		// Ids are trimmed and deduplicated, and unknown ids are ignored: this
238		// list excludes exactly b. The first rotation therefore lands on a.
239		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil, " b ", "b", "ghost"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
240	
241		// An empty list selects exactly as if the field were absent: the rotation
242		// continues just after a to b — the excluded id from before is eligible.
243		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil), "b", "h2:2", 2)
244		assertPick(t, selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 1, nil, []string{}...), "c", "h3:3", 3)
245	
246		// The failed validations never moved the cursor: the next plain selection
247		// wraps past c to a rather than restarting anywhere.
248		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 1)
249	}

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6		"testing"
7	)
8	
9	// This file is the regression guard for running an excludeInstanceIds
10	// selection after the service's instance list has been REPLACED: the
11	// per-service rotation cursor intentionally survives the replacement, so a
12	// selection carrying an exclude list must continue just after the last
13	// actually rotated id — even when that id was removed by the replacement —
14	// instead of restarting at the smallest id. The exclusion itself stays scoped
15	// to its one request: it neither degrades the excluded instance's health
16	// record nor removes it from the service. These tests lock the contract
17	// purely through the public Validate/Apply/Select and Snapshot results:
18	//
19	//   - with a, b, c, d healthy and the cursor resting on b, replacing the list
20	//     (removing b, keeping every other id and address) leaves the position on
21	//     the removed b: excluding c chooses d, the next plain selection wraps to
22	//     a, and the one after chooses the previously excluded c;
23	//   - every successful pick reports the post-replacement revision and the
24	//     address and accepted health sequence of the instance actually chosen;
25	//   - the replacement keeps the surviving instances' health records, and the
26	//     exclude request changes none of them;
27	//   - the instance submission order, in the original registration and in the
28	//     replacement, does not change the selection results;
29	//   - a selection using the pre-replacement revision is a conflict naming
30	//     both revisions, and excluding every healthy instance is no_healthy
31	//     naming the exclusion; both failures report the current revision,
32	//     fabricate no target, and move no cursor, so the next valid selection
33	//     continues just after the last actually rotated id.
34	
35	// runReplaceExcludeScenario drives the shared replacement-plus-exclusion
36	// scenario against a fresh registry with the given instance submission orders
37	// and locks the full pick sequence and the final service state.
38	func runReplaceExcludeScenario(t *testing.T, initial, replacement []Instance) {
39		t.Helper()
40		r := NewRegistry()
41		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, initial)
42		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 11, true, "")
43		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 12, true, "")
44		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 13, true, "")
45		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "d", 1, 14, true, "")
46	
47		// Ordinary selections take a then b; the cursor rests on b.
48		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 11)
49		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 12)
50	
51		// Replace the list at the current revision: b is removed, every other
52		// instance keeps its id and address. The replacement bumps the revision.
53		reg, err := r.ValidateRegistration("svc", 1, replacement)
54		if err != nil {
55			t.Fatalf("validate replacement: %v", err)
56		}
57		if out := r.Apply(reg); !out.OK || !out.Changed || out.Revision != 2 {
58			t.Fatalf("replacement must succeed and bump the revision to 2: %+v", out)
59		}
60	
61		// assertPickRev additionally locks that the pick reports the
62		// post-replacement revision, not the stale pre-replacement one.
63		assertPickRev := func(out SelectOutcome, id, addr string, seq int64) {
64			t.Helper()
65			assertPick(t, out, id, addr, seq)
66			if out.Revision != 2 {
67				t.Fatalf("select must report the post-replacement revision 2, got %+v", out)
68			}
69		}
70	
71		// Excluding c continues just after the removed b: d is chosen with its own
72		// address and accepted sequence. The position neither restarts at the
73		// smallest id (a) nor skips to the excluded c.
74		assertPickRev(selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 2, nil, "c"), "d", "h4:4", 14)
75		// A plain selection wraps past the end to a, and the one after chooses c:
76		// the exclusion was scoped to its one request and never removed c from the
77		// rotation.
78		assertPickRev(selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "a", "h1:1", 11)
79		assertPickRev(selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "c", "h3:3", 13)
80	
81		// The exclusion changed nothing durable: the revision is the replaced one,
82		// b is gone, and the surviving instances keep the health records accepted
83		// before the replacement — c in particular is still healthy at sequence 13.
84		if rev := r.RevisionOf("svc"); rev != 2 {
85			t.Fatalf("revision after replacement: %d", rev)
86		}
87		views := r.Snapshot()
88		if len(views) != 1 || views[0].Service != "svc" || views[0].Revision != 2 {
89			t.Fatalf("service view: %+v", views)
90		}
91		want := []InstanceView{
92			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1", Health: HealthHealthy, Sequence: 11},
93			{ID: "c", Address: "h3:3", Health: HealthHealthy, Sequence: 13},
94			{ID: "d", Address: "h4:4", Health: HealthHealthy, Sequence: 14},
95		}
96		if len(views[0].Instances) != len(want) {
97			t.Fatalf("instances: %+v", views[0].Instances)
98		}
99		for i := range want {
100			if views[0].Instances[i] != want[i] {
101				t.Fatalf("instance %d: got %+v want %+v", i, views[0].Instances[i], want[i])
102			}
103		}
104	}
105	
106	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeAfterReplacementKeepsRotation locks the main
107	// scenario: the exclude-carrying selection after the replacement continues
108	// the rotation from the removed b rather than restarting, and the exclusion
109	// leaves no durable trace. The whole scenario runs under two different
110	// instance submission orders — for the original registration and for the
111	// replacement — and must produce the identical pick sequence, because the
112	// rotation runs by ascending id, never by submission order.
113	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeAfterReplacementKeepsRotation(t *testing.T) {
114		orders := []struct {
115			initial     []Instance
116			replacement []Instance
117		}{
118			{
119				initial: []Instance{
120					{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
121					{ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
122				},
123				replacement: []Instance{
124					{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
125				},
126			},
127			{
128				initial: []Instance{
129					{ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
130					{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
131				},
132				replacement: []Instance{
133					{ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"}, {ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
134				},
135			},
136		}
137		for i, tc := range orders {
138			t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("submission order %d", i+1), func(t *testing.T) {
139				runReplaceExcludeScenario(t, tc.initial, tc.replacement)
140			})
141		}
142	}
143	
144	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeFailuresAfterReplacementKeepPosition locks the
145	// failure shapes after the replacement and their effect on the position: a
146	// selection carrying the pre-replacement revision conflicts with both
147	// revisions, and a correct-revision selection excluding every healthy
148	// instance is no_healthy with a reason naming the exclusion. Both report the
149	// current revision and fabricate no target id, address or sequence, and
150	// neither moves the cursor — the next valid selection continues just after
151	// the last actually rotated id.
152	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeFailuresAfterReplacementKeepPosition(t *testing.T) {
153		r := NewRegistry()
154		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
155			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
156			{ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
157		})
158		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 11, true, "")
159		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 12, true, "")
160		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 13, true, "")
161		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "d", 1, 14, true, "")
162	
163		// The cursor rests on b, which the replacement then removes.
164		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 11)
165		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 12)
166		registerService(t, r, "svc", 1, []Instance{
167			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
168		})
169	
170		assertNoTarget := func(out SelectOutcome) {
171			t.Helper()
172			if out.InstanceID != "" || out.Address != "" || out.Sequence != 0 {
173				t.Fatalf("failed select must fabricate no target, got id=%q addr=%q seq=%d",
174					out.InstanceID, out.Address, out.Sequence)
175			}
176		}
177	
178		// A caller still using the pre-replacement revision gets a conflict that
179		// states the expected and actual revisions and reports the current one.
180		sel, err := r.ValidateSelection("svc", 1)
181		if err != nil {
182			t.Fatalf("validate stale-revision select: %v", err)
183		}
184		out := r.Select(sel)
185		if out.OK || out.Kind != OutcomeConflict ||
186			out.Expected != 1 || out.Actual != 2 || out.Revision != 2 {
187			t.Fatalf("stale revision must conflict with both revisions: %+v", out)
188		}
189		if !strings.Contains(out.Reason, "revision 2, not 1") {
190			t.Fatalf("conflict reason must state both revisions, got %q", out.Reason)
191		}
192		assertNoTarget(out)
193	
194		// The correct revision with every healthy instance excluded is no_healthy;
195		// the reason says the exclusion removed them all.
196		out = selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 2, nil, "a", "c", "d")
197		if out.OK || out.Kind != OutcomeNoHealthy || out.Revision != 2 {
198			t.Fatalf("excluding every healthy instance must be no_healthy at the current revision: %+v", out)
199		}
200		if !strings.Contains(out.Reason, "excludeInstanceIds") {
201			t.Fatalf("no_healthy reason must say the exclusion removed every healthy instance, got %q", out.Reason)
202		}
203		assertNoTarget(out)
204	
205		// Both failures left the cursor on the removed b: the next valid selection
206		// continues just after it and picks c — not d, which would mean skipping
207		// the instance that was due, and not a, which would mean restarting from
208		// the smallest id.
209		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "c", "h3:3", 13)
210		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "d", "h4:4", 14)
211	}

1	package indexroom
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5		"testing"
6	)
7	
8	// This file is the regression guard for the release_session request: an
9	// explicit operation that drops ONE session binding in ONE service, so the
10	// key's next selection joins the normal rotation again.
11	//
12	// The lifecycle locked here, observed entirely through public results:
13	//
14	//   - releasing a bound key reports changed and deletes only that binding; the
15	//     key's next successful selection rotates from just after the last
16	//     actually rotated position (not from the smallest id and not from the
17	//     released binding) and records a fresh binding on success;
18	//   - releasing a key that has no binding still succeeds, without changed;
19	//   - the bound instance being removed, unknown, unhealthy, or the service
20	//     holding an empty instance list never blocks removing the binding — a
21	//     binding is only a remembered id;
22	//   - other sessions keep their bindings even when bound to the same
23	//     instance, and the same key in another service is a different binding;
24	//   - the release moves neither the rotation cursor nor any health record,
25	//     and never bumps the registration revision;
26	//   - revision/conflict/not_found failures state the current revision and
27	//     preserve the binding, and invalid fields (in particular a missing,
28	//     null-like or blank sessionKey) are reported before the revision check.
29	
30	// releaseSession validates and applies one release_session request, failing
31	// the test when validation itself rejects it (validation cases have their own
32	// test below).
33	func releaseSession(t *testing.T, r *Registry, service string, revision int64, key string) ReleaseOutcome {
34		t.Helper()
35		rel, err := r.ValidateSessionRelease(service, revision, &key)
36		if err != nil {
37			t.Fatalf("validate release %s key %q: %v", service, key, err)
38		}
39		return r.ReleaseSession(rel)
40	}
41	
42	// TestRegistryReleaseSessionRejoinsRotationAfterCursor locks the headline
43	// contract: after binding s -> a and a plain rotation to b, releasing s does
44	// not move the cursor, so the key's next selection continues just after b and
45	// lands on c rather than restarting at a. The success establishes a new
46	// binding, which later requests reuse.
47	func TestRegistryReleaseSessionRejoinsRotationAfterCursor(t *testing.T) {
48		r := NewRegistry()
49		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
50			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
51		})
52		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
53		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
54		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")
55	
56		// First session success rotates to the smallest id and binds s -> a; the
57		// shared cursor rests on a.
58		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
59	
60		// A plain selection advances the shared cursor to b.
61		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 2)
62	
63		// Releasing the binding reports changed, with the current revision and no
64		// target fields.
65		rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s")
66		if !rel.OK || !rel.Changed || rel.Revision != 1 {
67			t.Fatalf("release of the bound key: %+v", rel)
68		}
69		if rel.Kind != "" || rel.Reason != "" || rel.Expected != 0 || rel.Actual != 0 {
70			t.Fatalf("successful release must carry no failure fields: %+v", rel)
71		}
72	
73		// The key's next selection behaves like a first binding: it rotates from
74		// the last real position (just after b) and lands on c.
75		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
76	
77		// The fresh selection rebound the key: the next request reuses c without
78		// rotating, and a plain select continues just after c (wrapping to a).
79		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
80		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 1)
81		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
82	}
83	
84	// TestRegistryReleaseSessionWithoutBindingSucceeds locks that releasing a key
85	// that was never bound (or one already released) is still a success with no
86	// changed field and no revision bump.
87	func TestRegistryReleaseSessionWithoutBindingSucceeds(t *testing.T) {
88		r := NewRegistry()
89		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}})
90		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
91	
92		rel := releaseSession(t, r, "  svc  ", 1, "  ghost  ")
93		if !rel.OK || rel.Changed || rel.Revision != 1 || rel.Service != "svc" {
94			t.Fatalf("releasing an unbound key: %+v", rel)
95		}
96	
97		// The no-op release moved neither cursor nor state: a keyed selection with
98		// the released name rotates from scratch (smallest id) and binds, exactly
99		// as any first use would.
100		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "ghost"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
101	
102		// Releasing again now that the key is bound reports changed, and a third
103		// release is back to unchanged — idempotent from the second call on.
104		if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "ghost"); !rel.OK || !rel.Changed {
105			t.Fatalf("second release should remove the fresh binding: %+v", rel)
106		}
107		if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "ghost"); !rel.OK || rel.Changed {
108			t.Fatalf("third release must succeed unchanged: %+v", rel)
109		}
110	}
111	
112	// TestRegistryReleaseSessionIgnoresBoundInstanceState locks every
113	// cannot-block condition: the bound instance removed by a replacement,
114	// currently unhealthy, or the instance list emptied entirely — the binding
115	// itself still comes off and reports changed in all of them.
116	func TestRegistryReleaseSessionIgnoresBoundInstanceState(t *testing.T) {
117		t.Run("bound instance unhealthy", func(t *testing.T) {
118			r := NewRegistry()
119			registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}})
120			markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
121			markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 1, true, "")
122			assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
123	
124			// a is unhealthy: selection could not reuse the binding, but release
125			// must still remove it.
126			markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 2, false, "down")
127			if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"); !rel.OK || !rel.Changed || rel.Revision != 1 {
128				t.Fatalf("release against an unhealthy bound instance: %+v", rel)
129			}
130			// Nothing healthy but b: a fresh rotation from the cursor (still on a,
131			// the only real rotation) continues to b, proving the binding is gone.
132			assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "b", "h2:2", 1)
133		})
134	
135		t.Run("bound instance removed", func(t *testing.T) {
136			r := NewRegistry()
137			registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}})
138			markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
139			markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 1, true, "")
140			assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
141	
142			// Replace a away (content change bumps to revision 2).
143			registerService(t, r, "svc", 1, []Instance{{ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}})
144			if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 2, "s"); !rel.OK || !rel.Changed || rel.Revision != 2 {
145				t.Fatalf("release pointing at a removed instance: %+v", rel)
146			}
147		})
148	
149		t.Run("never confirmed healthy", func(t *testing.T) {
150			r := NewRegistry()
151			// Build the binding to a, then replace the list with the same ids at a
152			// NEW address only for a: a resets to unknown/0, while the binding
153			// still names a. Releasing must succeed despite the unknown target.
154			registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}})
155			markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
156			assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
157			registerService(t, r, "svc", 1, []Instance{{ID: "a", Address: "h9:9"}})
158			if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "a"); inst.Health != HealthUnknown || inst.Sequence != 0 {
159				t.Fatalf("a should be unknown/0 after the address change: %+v", inst)
160			}
161			if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 2, "s"); !rel.OK || !rel.Changed || rel.Revision != 2 {
162				t.Fatalf("release pointing at an unknown rebound instance: %+v", rel)
163			}
164		})
165	
166		t.Run("empty instance list", func(t *testing.T) {
167			r := NewRegistry()
168			registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}})
169			markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
170			assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
171	
172			// Empty the list: the service survives at revision 2, and releasing on
173			// it must still remove the dangling binding.
174			registerService(t, r, "svc", 1, nil)
175			if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 2, "s"); !rel.OK || !rel.Changed || rel.Revision != 2 {
176				t.Fatalf("release on an empty-list service: %+v", rel)
177			}
178			// A repeat release on the emptied service is an unchanged success, not
179			// not_found: the service still exists at its real revision.
180			if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 2, "s"); !rel.OK || rel.Changed {
181				t.Fatalf("repeat release on the emptied service: %+v", rel)
182			}
183		})

273	// TestRegistryReleaseSessionFailuresPreserveBinding locks the revision gate
274	// shared with health and select: a mismatch conflicts carrying both revisions,
275	// an unknown service at expectedRevision 0 is not_found, and either failure
276	// leaves the existing binding and cursor exactly as they were for the next
277	// request in the batch.
278	func TestRegistryReleaseSessionFailuresPreserveBinding(t *testing.T) {
279		r := NewRegistry()
280		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}})
281		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
282		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
283		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
284	
285		// Wrong revision on an existing service: conflict carrying current 1 and
286		// the submitted revision; the binding survives.
287		if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "svc", 9, "s"); rel.OK || rel.Kind != OutcomeConflict ||
288			rel.Expected != 9 || rel.Actual != 1 || rel.Revision != 1 || rel.Changed || rel.Reason == "" {
289			t.Fatalf("wrong revision release: %+v", rel)
290		}
291		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "s"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
292	
293		// Unknown service, non-zero revision: conflict against actual revision 0.
294		if rel := releaseSession(t, r, "ghost", 3, "s"); rel.OK || rel.Kind != OutcomeConflict ||
295			rel.Expected != 3 || rel.Actual != 0 || rel.Revision != 0 || rel.Reason == "" {
296			t.Fatalf("unknown service wrong revision: %+v", rel)
297		}
298	
299		// Unknown service, expectedRevision 0: not_found at revision 0.
